label: Relief reversed
summary: Monday's market relief did not last. Taiwan's Taiex fell as much as 7.9% and Korea's Kospi more than 6% as doubts about the AI boom returned, though the Dow rose on Tuesday and Brent slipped below $90. The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi-held Hodeidah after the Houthis threatened Saudi Red Sea ports. Putin called retaliation for Ukrainian refinery strikes inevitable, and gunmen held shoppers hostage in Cartagena. UNAIDS warned of unravelling HIV gains, the WHO urged an end to the US fuel blockade on Cuba, and California braced for its highest tides since 1983. Elsewhere tension eased: a rebel group said it had halted its advance on Bunia in Ebola-hit Ituri, and Australia and Solomon Islands signed a treaty. A Pakistani became the first foreign astronaut aboard Tiangong, and a Brazilian dengue trial cut cases sharply. The weighted formula gave 39; no editorial adjustment.
